findings.message:
[P2] Update README for restored 30-day token policy

Restoring `accessTokenMaxTtlMs` to 30 days makes the public contract in `README.md` stale: lines 127-129 still say newly issued access tokens are capped at 15 minutes, line 138 says retired keys are published for at most 15 minutes, line 189 caps exchanged agent tokens at 15 minutes, and line 210 calls 15 minutes the revocation fallback. Operators and JWT-only consumers reading those sections will rely on a bound that no longer exists; update them to the 15-minute default and 30-day maximum and 30-day overlap, or explicitly document that introspection is required.

src/auth_config.ts:130-131

summary: The code restores the documented 30-day access-token maximum and adds regression coverage for issuance, key overlap, and authorization-version rejection; only the public README still advertises the removed 15-minute cap.

evidence: `src/auth_config.ts:129-131` keeps the 15-minute default and restores the 30-day maximum, matching `docs/DECISIONS.md` and the 30-day cap in `docs/agent-login.md`.
`tests/passport_cutover_test.ts:258-346` adds regression coverage for 30-day issuance, normal key-rotation overlap, and authorization-version rejection through `/api/auth/session/me`.
`src/config_test.ts:229-244` and `tests/bun_test.ts:1225-1239` update requested-TTL bounds so 30-day and 365-day requests cap at 30 days while the default remains 15 minutes.
`tests/worker_runtime.mjs:1147-1149` and `1257-1263` distinguish the 15-minute SSO default from the 12-hour password-login token.
